Director: Alex Garland Writer: Alex Garland Cast: Alicia Vikander as Ava Domhnall Gleeson as Caleb Oscar Isaac as Nathan Sonoya Mizuno as Kyoko Synopsis:A young programmer is selected to participate in a ground-breaking experiment in artificial intelligence by evaluating the human qualities of a breath-taking female A.I.

Spoiler free review by me: Ex Machinia was a movie that kind of went under the radar for a long time for me and, I assume, for a lot of others. Trailers were released about a year before its initial release and then were taken down not long after that. Because of that a lot of people questioned if this movie even existed for quite a long time. Finally things started to pick up and a new trailer came out along with amazing reviews and it finally got on my radar. I waited for the wide release for I can't even tell you how long and saw it the very first day I could in theatres.

This time instead of staring with the actors I'm going to have to start with the writer/director Alex Garland. This is Garland's directorial debut and I have to say he was absolutely fantastic with this film. The script was incredibly well written. Every word spoken just felt so natural and even though this movie leaves you guessing until the last second he really does a good job of explaining things through the characters almost as soon as you have that question yourself. There were times where I was watching this movie and I would ask myself a question and literally the next scene answers it for me in detail. You can tell every part of this movie was incredibly well thought out by Garland himself and that's what movies need right now. The directing by Garland was also incredible, every shot was focused, the intense scenes were filmed to be intense while the more light hearted scenes were just fun to watch. Overall I have to say amazing job by Garland and you have earned yourself a life time follower if you keep up work like this.

So now onto acting. I have to admit I didn't know most of the actors in this film. Oscar Isaac and Domhnall Gleeson are both going to be starting in star wars episode 7 while Alicia Vikander will be starting alongside Henry Cavill and Armie Hammer later this summer in The Man From U.N.C.L.E. Alicia Vikander really stole the show as Ava. She's just so mesmerising and manipulative in this role it really show how much range she has as an upcoming young actress. When you first meet her you get this sweet, innocent young AI who just wants a friend in Caleb. Her character goes through so much you really start to wonder if you can actually trust her or not. Oscar Isaac plays the big boss, he's the man who created this AI known as Ava. Isaac really does an amazing job of playing this egotistical young tech genius. He's a lonely drunk who thinks he is a god for what he's done. Isaac really brings this home with his monologues and twisting of Gleeson's words. Domhnall Gleeson plays Nathan, a young coder who works at Caleb's company blue book. Nathan is supposed to be an innocent character who shows the good side of humanity. Gleeson does an amazing job of portraying this as he first meets Ava and really seems to fall for her innocence.

Overall this is one of my favorite movies of the year and I really hope it gets some recognition at the Oscar's, especially for Garlands work. I have to give this movie a 10/10 because I could not stop talking about it after seeing it. It really makes you think constantly and keeps you guessing until the last second. I cannot recommend this movie enough and if you haven't seen it you need to see it as soon as possible.
